briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 14, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Climate Crisis: Global Warnings and Deepening Impacts
sections.content: Today's news highlights prominent warning messages underscoring the severity of the global climate crisis. Specifically, the Himalayan megaflood has been identified as a 'time bomb' of global warming, raising concerns that the very foundations of civilization could collapse [6, 10]. Global warming is severing a 400-year climate connection between two oceans [37], and ancient British gardens and apple orchards worldwide are also threatened by extreme heat due to climate change [39, 43]. Prince William has warned that 'gradual' measures alone are insufficient to combat climate change [38], and even Bronze Age artifacts are at risk of permanent loss due to climate change [50]. This situation underscores the urgent need to shift wildfire response strategies from 'extinction' to 'prevention' [1].

sections.title: 🌱 Efforts to Enhance Climate Change Adaptation and Resilience
sections.content: Amidst this crisis, various efforts are underway to explore adaptation and mitigation strategies for climate change [2]. Domestically, joint tracking of subtropical fish species and harmful organisms in Korean and Japanese waters is strengthening responses to fishery resources in the face of climate change [3], and Cheongyang log shiitake mushroom farms are striving to protect their production base beyond climate change [4]. Research is also underway to find agricultural solutions for the era of climate crisis through small Antarctic flowers [5], and the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education is distributing an 'Ecological Transition Project' toolkit, which seeks climate crisis solutions in schools, to raise awareness among future generations [9]. Internationally, storm-battered Hawaiian communities are seeking more resilient solutions [40], and some global cities are showing positive signs by demonstrating strong preparedness for climate change [42].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Expansion of Domestic Carbon Neutrality Policies and Community Participation
sections.content: Various local governments and institutions across the country are achieving tangible results in realizing carbon neutrality. Seoul's Gwanak-gu district received the Minister's Award for Best Practices in 2026 for its life-oriented carbon neutrality policies [12, 16, 17, 18], and Buk-gu district of Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Metropolitan City also received a Minister's Award in recognition of its achievements in practicing carbon neutrality in daily life [21, 26]. The Korea Food Industry Association and the Korea Energy Agency have signed a business agreement to promote solar power and energy efficiency in the food sector, supporting companies' transition to carbon neutrality [7, 22]. Furthermore, resident-led carbon neutrality policy proposals and practical activities are actively underway, including approximately 200 citizens advocating for carbon neutrality by bicycle in downtown Daegu [23] [13, 24, 25].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Facing Challenges
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is accelerating globally, and its economic benefits are also being proven. It has been confirmed that renewable energy has saved 4.4 trillion won in fossil fuel electricity purchase costs over the past five months, acting as an energy shock mitigator [29]. China is forming two pillars of renewable energy growth through government support and market competition [27], and is presenting solar and wind power storage solutions and a blueprint for zero-carbon cities through solid hydrogen technology [20]. Domestically, the adoption of renewable energy is expanding, with Jeju Samdasoo beginning water intake using eco-friendly electricity [31]. However, policy challenges for expanding renewable energy deployment still exist, such as the issue of wind power subsidies being allocated to regions other than where the actual power generation occurs [34].

sections.title: 🌍 Raising Climate Crisis Awareness and Leadership in the International Community
sections.content: In the international community, efforts to raise awareness and demonstrate leadership regarding the climate crisis are ongoing. Prince William expressed 'urgent optimism' that the tide of the climate crisis can be turned by 2030, urging action from the international community [41, 46]. The importance of solving climate issues through inter-state cooperation is also emphasized, as exemplified by the Minister of Environment and Climate Change holding talks with the Eritrean Ambassador [45]. The Royal BC Museum is raising public awareness through an exhibition showcasing how climate change is transforming British Columbia (B.C.) [47]. These efforts contribute to building international consensus and driving behavioral change in response to climate change.

briefing.closing: As we have seen in today's briefing, amidst escalating warnings of a global climate crisis, various mitigation and adaptation efforts are continuing both domestically and internationally. It is urgent to accelerate the transition to renewable energy and achieve carbon neutrality in cooperation with local communities. This concludes today's climate briefing.
